description: Return DDS participant lifecycle events (`discovered` / `lost`) from a recent window, e.g. 'who left in the last 5 minutes?', as a `ParticipantEventListing`, newest first: `guid`, `event_type`, `vendor`, `timestamp_ns`, `time_source`, `observed_ns`, `age_s` (seconds before the response; live only), optional `name` (announced name), `hostname` and `domain_id`. `time_source` is `dds_source_timestamp` (timestamp of the announcement or dispose) or `observed_local` (when TopicForge noticed, weakest). **Crash caveat**: a `lost` timestamp is an upper bound of the death: exact after a clean shutdown, the lease expiry after a crash, so the process died up to one lease earlier (10 s Cyclone, 20 s Fast DDS, 100 s RTI); the two cases cannot be told apart. **Restarts**: a restarted node is a new participant (one `lost` and one `discovered`, different `guid`, same `name`); `restarts_by_name` gives `lives` and `departures` per name over the window, so do not count GUIDs by hand. Capped at 200 events (`truncated`, `note`; reduce `lookback_s`). TopicForge only knows what happened since it started watching (`health_check.observer_started_ns`). **Backends**: Fast DDS uses listener callbacks; Cyclone polls discovery in the background every 0.5 s, so a participant cycle faster than the reader's history depth between two passes can be missed; mock returns a fixture timeline. Right after start the call waits up to 3 s for discovery. **Read-only by architecture**. **Raises an MCP error** when no DDS module is active. **Duration**: uses the DDS binding behind the DDS lock (one call at a time); the whole call, lock wait included, ends within 45 s, and if another DDS call holds the lock it fails at once with a `busy` error (retry).

domain_id.description: Ignored: it does not switch domains and is only range-checked (0..232). The domain observed is the one joined at startup (`TOPICFORGE_DDS_DOMAIN_ID`), reported in the response `domain_id`; `note` flags a different non-zero value.

lookback_s.description: Window in seconds, 1..86400, default 300. A larger window may hit the 200-event cap.

name: participant_events

departures.description: Times a participant with this name was lost.

lives.description: Distinct GUIDs that carried this name; restarts = `lives` - 1.

age_s.description: Seconds between `timestamp_ns` and this response; `None` in mock mode.

event_type.description: `discovered` (joined or rejoined) or `lost` (removed, or gone from discovery); reported once per change.

observed_ns.description: Local ns when TopicForge noticed the event, never before a DDS-derived `timestamp_ns`; `None` when untracked.

time_source.description: `dds_source_timestamp` (DDS timestamp of the announcement or dispose; for `lost` an upper bound of the death) or `observed_local` (when TopicForge noticed, weakest).

timestamp_ns.description: Wall-clock ns of the event; its origin is `time_source`.

restarts_by_name.description: Names seen with several GUIDs or lost at least once (absent: ran once and stayed). A restart is a new GUID with the same name. Window only.

restarts_note.description: Set when unnamed participants were left out of `restarts_by_name`.

truncated.description: True when cut to the 200-event cap.

title: DDS participant events
